hero.headline: I-95 closed in both directions in Indian River County after fatal trooper-involved shooting
hero.teaser: I-95 is closed in both directions in Indian River County following a trooper-involved shooting that ended with a suspect dead, authorities said. Northbound drivers are being direct
hero.body:
I-95 is closed in both directions in Indian River County following a trooper-involved shooting that ended with a suspect dead, authorities said. Northbound drivers are being directed off the interstate at Indrio Road, while southbound drivers are being directed to exit at Oslo Road.

 All northbound and southbound lanes are closed, along with the southbound entrance ramp at Oslo Road and the northbound entrance ramp from Indrio Road. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said the highway closure is due to the ongoing investigation.

 FHP said the shooting occurred around 11:20 p.m. near mile marker 141. The incident began when a trooper initiated a traffic stop and the suspect fled, leading to a pursuit, according to FHP. The pursuit escalated into an exchange of gunfire between the trooper and the suspect.

 The suspect suffered what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound and was pronounced dead at the scene, FHP said. Authorities said no troopers were injured. FDLE will take over as the lead agency in the investigation, and officials said all body camera and dash camera video will be reviewed.

cards.headline: Florida's Turnpike northbound closed in Palm City after truck crash
cards.teaser: A tractor-trailer and a pickup truck crashed near mile marker 137 Friday morning. Officials said both drivers are safe, and crews are working to clear debris.
cards.body:
The northbound lanes of Florida's Turnpike are closed near mile marker 137 in Palm City after a crash involving a tractor-trailer and a pickup truck Friday morning.

 The crash happened just before 11 a.m., according to Martin County Fire Rescue. Officials said both drivers are safe.

 Martin County Fire Rescue, the Martin County Sheriffs Office and Florida Highway Patrol are working to clear debris from the roadway. Drivers are being asked to avoid the area, seek alternate routes and expect delays.

cards.headline: Woman, 75, killed by pickup while crossing Seaway Drive in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police said Friday that a 75-year-old woman died after a pickup truck struck her while she was crossing Seaway Drive with her husband. The crash remains under investiga
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police said Friday that a 75-year-old woman died after a pickup truck struck her while she was crossing Seaway Drive with her husband. The crash remains under investigation, and police are asking anyone with information to come forward.

 Officers responded Wednesday to the 1100 block of Seaway Drive. Police determined the couple were crossing toward the Dockside Inn Resort when a westbound 2013 Ford F-150 pickup truck driven by a man struck the woman. Her husband was uninjured, police said. The woman was taken to a local hospital, where she was pronounced dead at approximately 7 p.m.

 Anyone with information about the crash is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

cards.headline: Collin O’Hara sentenced to life for 2020 killing of Calvin Bates in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A judge denied the defense’s request for a reduced sentence. O’Hara will receive credit for 3,341 days already served.
cards.body:
Collin O’Hara was sentenced to life in prison Tuesday for the 2020 killing of Calvin Bates in Fort Pierce, with the judge denying the defense’s request for a reduced sentence. A jury found O’Hara guilty of second-degree murder. He will receive credit for 3,341 days already served.

 Fort Pierce police found Bates on a rear patio at an apartment complex at 601 Avenue B on June 12, 2020, with a knife in his neck. Bates later died during surgery at Lawnwood Hospital.

 According to the arrest affidavit, a witness told investigators O’Hara accused Bates of being a child rapist before stabbing him. Another witness said she saw O’Hara’s arm move toward Bates’ neck, then saw the knife in Bates’ neck as O’Hara left.

 Police said O’Hara fled the scene and was arrested at an Anytime Fitness on Orange Avenue. During an interview with investigators, O’Hara denied stabbing Bates, according to the affidavit.

cards.headline: Stuart Air Show access: Monterey Road entrances, free parking at Witham Field
cards.teaser: Visitors can use two drive-in entrances off Monterey Road, with free designated parking and complimentary shuttles to the main gates.
cards.body:
Visitors heading to the Stuart Air Show at Witham Field will have two drive-in entrances off Monterey Road, free general parking in designated areas and complimentary shuttles to the main gates. The Martin County Sheriff's Office will direct traffic around the air show, which is preparing to bring aircraft, crowds and heavier traffic to the Stuart area.

 Drivers coming from Interstate 95 can take the Stuart exit and follow Kanner Highway to Monterey Road. Those using Florida's Turnpike can take Southwest Martin Downs Boulevard. Dixie Highway is another option for reaching Monterey Road. As visitors approach Witham Field, they should follow posted signs and directions from law enforcement.

 General parking is free in designated Stuart Air Show parking areas, and ADA parking is available. Complimentary shuttles will carry visitors from the parking areas to the main gates. Drivers should use the official parking lots rather than create their own spaces or park outside designated areas.

 The Stuart Air Show is celebrating its 37th year at Witham Field. Lee Potter with the Stuart Air Show said this year's event will feature the F-16 demo team, along with a variety of other aircraft arriving throughout the week.

cards.headline: Newly released 911 account details gun allegations in September Palm City standoff
cards.teaser: A woman told dispatchers Darrel Abbey was chasing her with guns and had fired them. Newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property.
cards.body:
A newly released 911 call transcript adds details to September’s hourslong standoff in Palm City, with a woman telling dispatchers that Darrel Abbey was chasing her with guns and had fired them. The transcript, released through a public records request, describes the caller’s allegations during an incident that brought Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies, SWAT team members and hostage negotiators to the home.

 The woman urged dispatchers to send help quickly and said she was running down the street. She described Abbey as intoxicated and said he had tried to get into a car. About an hour and a half earlier, she told the dispatcher, Abbey had put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger, but the gun did not fire. She said he was not in a good state of mind.

 As she ran, the caller said Abbey turned around and headed back toward the home. She stopped along the road, where another woman had pulled over to help her. The caller also said there were multiple guns at the property, though she was unsure whether they were inside the house, in a vehicle or in an RV.

 Separately, newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property during the response. The footage is partially obscured.

 According to the arrest report, Abbey’s ex-girlfriend went to his home after their breakup. She told investigators he appeared intoxicated and had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts. The report says he brought the guns inside, yelled at her and pointed a gun at her several times.

 It also says he later tried to get into his vehicle and reached for her phone when he realized she was recording. She ran down the road and called 911.

 Deputies later tried to contact Abbey at the home, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, according to the arrest report. He was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. The report identifies him as a convicted felon with a prior vehicular assault conviction in Washington state.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast traffic report: I-95 ramp closures, road work planned Nov. 13–20
hero.teaser: Overnight I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Oslo Road, Port St. Lucie side-street closures and resurfacing are on FDOT's Nov. 13–20 schedule.
hero.body:
Drivers across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties should prepare for another week of overnight I-95 work, ramp closures and daytime lane restrictions, according to the Florida Department of Transportation's traffic report for Nov. 13–20.

 The most significant disruptions begin Sunday night, Nov. 15. They include closures of both northbound I-95 ramps at SW Martin Highway in Martin County, four separately scheduled ramp closures at the new Oslo Road interchange in Indian River County, and extended neighborhood road closures along SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard.

 FDOT says roadwork schedules can change because of weather or unforeseen conditions. For live interstate traffic information, drivers can check FL511 ; updated construction information is available through FDOT District 4 .

 Biggest closures to know about

 I-95 northbound at SW Martin Highway, Exit 110, Martin County: The exit ramp and entrance ramp are each scheduled for overnight closures from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, through Thursday, Nov. 19 , for repaving. FDOT says only one of the affected ramps will close at a time. Signed detours will use Becker Road and nearby connecting roads.
- I-95 at Oslo Road, Exit 143, Indian River County: All four interchange ramps have separately scheduled overnight closures Sunday, Nov. 15, from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. Crews will stagger the closures so two ramps are not closed at the same time. Additional nights later in November and early December are designated as contingencies.
- SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard side streets: Extended closures are possible on SW Jaslo, Koler, McCoy, McCullough and McHord avenues and SW Paar Drive for drainage and utility installation.

 Work may start at 7 a.m. Monday, Nov. 16 , with affected roads reopening by 5 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20 .

 Adjacent streets will not close simultaneously, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.
- SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SW Fisherman and SW Liberty avenues: Full road closures may occur intermittently from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20 , for utility work. Detours will use SW Fisherman Avenue, SW Liberty Avenue and SW Pisano Street.
- I-95 mainline in Martin and St. Lucie counties: Overnight work will reduce portions of I-95 by as many as two lanes in each direction, including the Bridge Road-to-county-line stretch in Martin County and the Gatlin Boulevard-to-Becker Road stretch in St. Lucie County.
- Advance notice — I-95 at Kanner Highway, Exit 101: The southbound entrance and exit ramps are scheduled for separate overnight closures Nov. 30–Dec. 3 , outside this week's reporting window. Contingency dates are Dec. 6–10.

 Martin County

 I-95 ramp closures and overnight resurfacing

 I-95 between C.R. 708/SE Bridge Road and the Martin–St. Lucie county line: Two southbound lanes are scheduled to close from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. , and two northbound lanes from 8:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. , Sunday, Nov. 15, through Tuesday, Nov. 24. The work includes milling, resurfacing and signage improvements.

 Two overnight ramp closures are also scheduled at S.R. 714/SW Martin Highway, Exit 110 , Sunday, Nov. 15, through Thursday, Nov. 19:

 Northbound exit ramp to Martin Highway: Closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers will continue north to SW Becker Road, Exit 114 , travel west on Becker Road and take the southbound I-95 entrance ramp to reach the Martin Highway exit. Northbound entrance ramp from Martin Highway: Closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers will use eastbound Martin Highway, northbound SW Newfield Parkway and westbound SW Becker Road to enter northbound I-95 at Becker Road. FDOT says the ramp closures will occur one at a time, with signs directing motorists through the detours.

 Advance notice for Kanner Highway: The southbound I-95 entrance ramp from S.R. 76/SW Kanner Highway and the southbound I-95 exit to Kanner Highway, Exit 101 , are each scheduled for overnight closures from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 30 through Dec. 3. The entrance detour uses Kanner Highway, Pratt Whitney Road and Bridge Road; the exit detour sends drivers south to Bridge Road, Exit 96 , and back north toward Kanner Highway. Weather contingency dates are Dec. 6–10.

 U.S. 1, A1A and Martin Highway

 U.S. 1 in Hobe Sound, between SE Dixie Highway and SE Osprey Street: One northbound lane may close from 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. and again from 9 p.m. to 7 a.m. Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20. One southbound lane may close from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday, with additional overnight southbound restrictions from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, through Thursday, Nov. 19. Access to homes and businesses will be maintained as resurfacing and trail construction continue.
- S.R. A1A/NE Ocean Boulevard, from NE Shore Village Terrace toward the Jensen Beach Causeway: One lane may close intermittently in either direction Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20, for drainage and pavement-widening work. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic.
- S.R. 714/SW Martin Highway, between SW Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard: One lane may close intermittently from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, through Thursday, Nov. 19, for milling, resurfacing, roadway widening and light-pole installation. Flaggers will maintain traffic.

 Local maintenance and utility work

 Palm City — S.R. 718/SW Martin Highway between SW Martin Downs Boulevard and SW 42nd Avenue: One westbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20. Stuart — SE Monterey Road between U.S. 1 and SE Dixie Highway: Intermittent eastbound and westbound lane closures are planned from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday. Stuart — U.S. 1 between SE Indian Street and SE Monterey Road; NW 16th Street and NW 16th Place; and SE Monterey Road and Grumman Boulevard: Intermittent lane closures are scheduled from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday for utility work. Stuart — SW Kanner Highway between SW Gaines Avenue and SW Salerno Road: One northbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday. Stuart — NE Ocean Boulevard between Joe's Point Road and Tiger Shores Beach: One southbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday. Tequesta — U.S. 1 between SE Jupiter Inlet Way and Intracoastal Place: One lane may close in either direction from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20 , for paving work. St. Lucie County

 I-95 work near Becker Road, Gatlin Boulevard and Fort Pierce

 I-95 between SW Gatlin Boulevard and just south of SW Becker Road: Two northbound lanes may close from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. , and two southbound lanes from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. , Sunday, Nov. 15, through Friday, Nov. 20. Lane shifts are possible during resurfacing and pavement-marking work. I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and just south of S.R. 70/Okeechobee Road: Shoulder closures in both directions are scheduled from 6:30 a.m. to 7 p.m. , and up to two lanes may close overnight from 8 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. , Sunday, Nov. 15, through Friday, Nov. 20, for grading, signage, drill shafts and pavement markings. Port St. Lucie Boulevard and U.S. 1

 S.R. 716/SE Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SE Seafury Lane and SE Lennard Road: One lane may close intermittently from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20. Two lanes may close intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, through Friday, Nov. 20, for construction and striping. U.S. 1 between SE Jennings Road and NW Golden Oak Trail: One lane may close in either direction from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday and from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday. SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SW Jordin Avenue and SW Alcantarra Boulevard: One lane may close intermittently in either direction from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20, as the road-widening project continues. Extended neighborhood closures off SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard

 As part of the widening project, crews plan intermittent extended closures on neighborhood streets for drainage and utility installation. Affected roads may close beginning 7 a.m. Monday, Nov. 16 , and reopen by 5 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20 :

 SW Jaslo Avenue: Between SW Jacoby Avenue and SW Paar Drive. SW Koler Avenue: Between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Kober Road. SW McCoy Avenue: Between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Jamros Street. SW McCullough Avenue: Between SW Jaslo Avenue and SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard. SW McHord Avenue: Between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Kabane Street. SW Paar Drive: Eastbound between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW McCandless Street, and westbound between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Jaqust Street. Signed detours will direct drivers to nearby connecting streets. FDOT says neighboring road closures will not occur at the same time and residents and businesses will retain access during construction.

 In addition, SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard itself, between SW Fisherman Avenue and SW Liberty Avenue , may close intermittently overnight from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20 , while utility operations are underway. Northbound motorists will be directed west on Fisherman Avenue, north on Pisano Street and east on Liberty Avenue; southbound motorists will use Liberty Avenue, Pisano Street and Fisherman Avenue.

 North Causeway Bridge, Midway Road and U.S. 1

 The new S.R. A1A/E.C. Summerlin Family Bridge in Fort Pierce remains open to vehicles. The old drawbridge is being demolished, and related work continues along U.S. 1, Old Dixie Highway, Juanita Avenue and nearby streets.

 The north-side bicycle lanes and shared-use path remain closed; pedestrians should use the bridge's south-side sidewalk. The new bridge does not connect directly to Old Dixie Highway.

 Scheduled restrictions include:

 U.S. 1 between Juanita Avenue and Naco Road: One northbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays through November. Juanita Avenue west of U.S. 1: The westbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays through November, with flaggers assisting traffic. Harbortown Drive: One lane in either direction may close from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays through November. U.S. 1 between NE 3rd Street and Juanita Avenue: One northbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays through November. Old Dixie Highway between Sunny Lane and Juanita Avenue: One lane in either direction may close from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays, with reconstruction continuing through Dec. 18. **S.R. A1A from east of the E.C. Summerlin Family Bridge to Little Jim's Bridge: One lane in either direction may close from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Saturday through November.
- C.R. 712/Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road: One eastbound or westbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. weekdays and from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m.** Sunday night through Friday night as widening and resurfacing continue. A westbound traffic shift between NW Corporate Way and Selvitz Road remains in place.

 Port St. Lucie and Fort Pierce maintenance

 SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard: Overnight utility work may close a lane between SW Trenton Lane and SW Cameo Boulevard; SE Midport Road and SE Westmoreland Road; SW Best Street and SE Belvedere Street; SE Whitmore Drive and SE Wald Street; and SW Monterey Lane and SW Bayshore Boulevard . The listed hours are 9 p.m. to 4 a.m. Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20 . U.S. 1 in Port St. Lucie: Northbound daytime lane closures are listed between SE Huffman Road and Savanna Club Road , and SE Jennings Road and SE Village Drive , for utility work. Midway Road between NW East Torino Parkway and NW Corporate Way: Intermittent eastbound and westbound daytime lane closures are scheduled for utility installation. Fort Pierce — U.S. 1: Daytime northbound lane closures are listed near Ulrich Road, Sunshine Boulevard, Tropical Isles Way, Melton Drive, East Midway Road, Sandhill Boulevard and High Point Boulevard ; additional restrictions are listed near Pinewood Drive and Georgia Avenue for signal work. Fort Pierce — S.R. 70/Okeechobee Road: Intermittent daytime lane closures are scheduled on several segments, including areas near 11 Mile Road, Midway Road, Coolidge Road, Rock Road, Gordy Road and Matthews Road , for pole replacement. Fort Pierce — S. Kings Highway between Saint Lucie Boulevard and Indrio Road: Intermittent closures are scheduled from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday for utility work. Indian River County

 Four I-95 ramp closures at Oslo Road, Exit 143

 Four ramps at the I-95/Oslo Road interchange are scheduled for separate closures Sunday night, Nov. 15, from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. for shoulder paving and final asphalt work. FDOT says the closures will be staggered so no two ramps are shut down simultaneously:

 Northbound I-95 exit to Oslo Road: FDOT's written detour identifies S.R. 614/Indrio Road and 43rd Avenue SW/Johnston Road as connecting roads. Drivers should follow on-site detour signs; the report's referenced exit number is not a substitute for the posted route. Northbound I-95 entrance from westbound Oslo Road: Drivers will use northbound 82nd Avenue, westbound S.R. 60/20th Street , then enter northbound I-95. Southbound I-95 exit to Oslo Road: FDOT's written detour references S.R. 60/20th Street and 82nd Avenue to reach Oslo Road. Follow the marked detour and posted signs at the interchange.
- Southbound I-95 entrance from westbound Oslo Road: Drivers will be directed via 82nd Avenue, 43rd Avenue SW/Johnston Road and Indrio Road to reach southbound I-95. FDOT lists a separate truck detour.

 Additional dates, Nov. 16–19, Nov. 22–23 and Nov. 30–Dec. 3 , are set aside as contingency nights if needed. FDOT specifies no lane, shoulder or ramp closures for this project from Wednesday, Nov. 25, through midnight Sunday, Nov. 29 , to reduce Thanksgiving holiday impacts.

 Other I-95 and Oslo Road work includes intermittent rolling lane closures on I-95 and interchange ramps from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. on selected nights through Dec. 10. Some portions of I-95 near the interchange may have up to two lanes closed overnight for pavement markings, rumble strips, wrong-way detection testing and final work. Near Oslo Road, sections of 58th, 66th, 74th and 82nd avenues may also have nighttime lane restrictions, with flaggers maintaining traffic.

 Sebastian, 90th Avenue and Sebastian Inlet

 S.R. 510/90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street: One lane may close intermittently in each direction from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, through Friday, Nov. 20 , for construction. Advance notice — S.R. 510/90th Avenue: Extended full overnight closures are planned from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nov. 30–Dec. 3 for drainage work. Detours will use 85th Street, U.S. 1 and Sebastian Boulevard . Weather contingency dates are Dec. 6–10; homes and businesses will remain accessible.
- S.R. A1A/Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway at Sebastian Inlet: Traffic has been shifted to temporary pavement near the bridge as construction of the replacement bridge continues. The temporary pattern, introduced in October, is expected to remain through late 2028 .
- Sebastian Inlet Bridge work zone: One northbound or southbound lane and/or shoulder may close as needed from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Thursday , or **7 a.m. to 1 p.m.

 Friday , through November. Only one lane will close at a time; flaggers will direct vehicles.
- Sebastian Inlet State Park:** Portions of both the north and south parking lots remain partially closed for bridge construction. The park remains open, parking is limited, south-jetty access from the south lot is closed, and the boat ramp remains accessible.

 Vero Beach maintenance and utility work

 U.S. 1 between Vista Royale Boulevard and Spring Lake Drive: One northbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18 . U.S. 1 between 24th Street and 21st Street: One lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday, Nov. 16, through Friday, Nov. 20 . S.R. 60/20th Street between 66th Avenue and Indian Creek Boulevard, and between 94th Court and Americana Way: One eastbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday. U.S. 1 between Bridge Boulevard and Durrance Road, and between 61st Place and 63rd Street: One northbound lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday for sign installation. **S.R. A1A between Mango Road and Shoe Drive: One lane may close intermittently from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, through Thursday, Nov. 19 , for signal upgrades.
- Westbound S.R. 60 between 97th Road and 98th Avenue: The left-turn lane may close intermittently from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday.
- Eastbound S.R. 60 between 33rd Avenue and 26th Avenue: One lane may close from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.** Monday through Friday.

 These are scheduled construction and maintenance impacts, not real-time incident closures. FDOT says some restrictions may be canceled, postponed or adjusted. Check FL511 for current interstate conditions and FDOT District 4 for updated project and lane-closure information before traveling.

cards.headline: Stuart Air Show access: Monterey Road entrances, free parking at Witham Field
cards.teaser: Visitors can use two drive-in entrances off Monterey Road, with free designated parking and complimentary shuttles to the main gates.
cards.body:
Visitors heading to the Stuart Air Show at Witham Field will have two drive-in entrances off Monterey Road, free general parking in designated areas and complimentary shuttles to the main gates. The Martin County Sheriff's Office will direct traffic around the air show, which is preparing to bring aircraft, crowds and heavier traffic to the Stuart area.

 Drivers coming from Interstate 95 can take the Stuart exit and follow Kanner Highway to Monterey Road. Those using Florida's Turnpike can take Southwest Martin Downs Boulevard. Dixie Highway is another option for reaching Monterey Road. As visitors approach Witham Field, they should follow posted signs and directions from law enforcement.

 General parking is free in designated Stuart Air Show parking areas, and ADA parking is available. Complimentary shuttles will carry visitors from the parking areas to the main gates. Drivers should use the official parking lots rather than create their own spaces or park outside designated areas.

 The Stuart Air Show is celebrating its 37th year at Witham Field. Lee Potter with the Stuart Air Show said this year's event will feature the F-16 demo team, along with a variety of other aircraft arriving throughout the week.

cards.headline: Newly released 911 account details gun allegations in September Palm City standoff
cards.teaser: A woman told dispatchers Darrel Abbey was chasing her with guns and had fired them. Newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property.
cards.body:
A newly released 911 call transcript adds details to September’s hourslong standoff in Palm City, with a woman telling dispatchers that Darrel Abbey was chasing her with guns and had fired them. The transcript, released through a public records request, describes the caller’s allegations during an incident that brought Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies, SWAT team members and hostage negotiators to the home.

 The woman urged dispatchers to send help quickly and said she was running down the street. She described Abbey as intoxicated and said he had tried to get into a car. About an hour and a half earlier, she told the dispatcher, Abbey had put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger, but the gun did not fire. She said he was not in a good state of mind.

 As she ran, the caller said Abbey turned around and headed back toward the home. She stopped along the road, where another woman had pulled over to help her. The caller also said there were multiple guns at the property, though she was unsure whether they were inside the house, in a vehicle or in an RV.

 Separately, newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property during the response. The footage is partially obscured.

 According to the arrest report, Abbey’s ex-girlfriend went to his home after their breakup. She told investigators he appeared intoxicated and had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts. The report says he brought the guns inside, yelled at her and pointed a gun at her several times.

 It also says he later tried to get into his vehicle and reached for her phone when he realized she was recording. She ran down the road and called 911.

 Deputies later tried to contact Abbey at the home, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, according to the arrest report. He was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. The report identifies him as a convicted felon with a prior vehicular assault conviction in Washington state.

hero.headline: Woman, 75, killed by pickup while crossing Seaway Drive in Fort Pierce
hero.teaser: Fort Pierce police said Friday that a 75-year-old woman died after a pickup truck struck her while she was crossing Seaway Drive with her husband. The crash remains under investiga
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police said Friday that a 75-year-old woman died after a pickup truck struck her while she was crossing Seaway Drive with her husband. The crash remains under investigation, and police are asking anyone with information to come forward.

 Officers responded Wednesday to the 1100 block of Seaway Drive. Police determined the couple were crossing toward the Dockside Inn Resort when a westbound 2013 Ford F-150 pickup truck driven by a man struck the woman. Her husband was uninjured, police said. The woman was taken to a local hospital, where she was pronounced dead at approximately 7 p.m.

 Anyone with information about the crash is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

cards.headline: Sheriff seeks help identifying suspect in Fort Pierce store burglary
cards.teaser: Investigators say a man stole about $3,200 in cash and merchandise from MLK Food Corner Store before fleeing on foot east on Kentucky Avenue.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is asking for help identifying a man accused of burglarizing MLK Food Corner Store in Fort Pierce. Investigators estimate about $3,200 in cash and merchandise was stolen from the business on South 33rd Street.

 The burglary happened around 3:45 a.m., according to investigators. Deputies said the suspect entered the store, took cash from the register and filled a bag with smoking-related merchandise before leaving. Authorities said he fled on foot and was last seen heading east on Kentucky Avenue.

 Anyone who recognizes the suspect or has information about the case is urged to contact the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office at 772-462-7300 or email Patroltips@stluciesheriff.com.

hero.headline: I-95 closed in both directions in Indian River County after fatal trooper-involved shooting
hero.teaser: I-95 is closed in both directions in Indian River County following a trooper-involved shooting that ended with a suspect dead, authorities said. Northbound drivers are being direct
hero.body:
I-95 is closed in both directions in Indian River County following a trooper-involved shooting that ended with a suspect dead, authorities said. Northbound drivers are being directed off the interstate at Indrio Road, while southbound drivers are being directed to exit at Oslo Road.

 All northbound and southbound lanes are closed, along with the southbound entrance ramp at Oslo Road and the northbound entrance ramp from Indrio Road. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said the highway closure is due to the ongoing investigation.

 FHP said the shooting occurred around 11:20 p.m. near mile marker 141. The incident began when a trooper initiated a traffic stop and the suspect fled, leading to a pursuit, according to FHP. The pursuit escalated into an exchange of gunfire between the trooper and the suspect.

 The suspect suffered what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound and was pronounced dead at the scene, FHP said. Authorities said no troopers were injured. FDLE will take over as the lead agency in the investigation, and officials said all body camera and dash camera video will be reviewed.
